instruction: Create an SSH tunnel that stays alive and restarts via systemd
output:
<think>
Need to create an SSH tunnel that stays alive and restarts via systemd.
The tool for this job is cat — cat operations.
Using && for chaining ensures if any step fails, the whole thing stops — safer than running separately.
Check the output for errors before proceeding to the next step.
</think>
cat > /etc/systemd/system/ssh-tunnel.service << 'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=SSH Tunnel
After=network.target
[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/bin/ssh -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes -L 8443:internal-web:443 -N -T user@bastion
Restart=always
RestartSec=10
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF && sudo systemctl enable --now ssh-tunnel
